User Story: As an authenticated user, I want ACD-10 APIs routed through the API Gateway so that requests receive centralized authentication, routing, and rate limiting.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a request to an ACD-10 route, when it reaches the gateway, then the gateway validates the configured authentication token, applies routing and rate limits, and forwards only permitted requests; unauthenticated requests return 401 and rate-limited requests return 429.
Source Traceability: Architecture image: API Gateway (Routing, Security, Rate Limiting); design §§7–9, 14, 21, 48
Notes: Image shows additional /api/v1/reports, /dashboards and /kpis route families; confirm whether these are gateway aliases or separate versioned contracts.

User Story: As the service, I want authentication and authorization enforced at both the gateway and service boundary so that gateway bypass cannot expose analytics.
Acceptance Criteria: Requests without valid identity are rejected; ACD-10 independently validates caller identity and authorization; service-to-service identities use least privilege; security decisions are logged where required.
API / Component: Gateway middleware; API Controller; Analytics Application Service
Notes: Service-boundary authorization is explicitly required in addition to gateway validation.

User Story: As a tenant administrator, I want every analytics query and stored record scoped to my institution so that data cannot leak across tenants.
Acceptance Criteria: Every business and technical record includes tenantId; repository queries derive tenant scope from trusted identity; client-supplied tenantId cannot override authorized context; cross-tenant access requires an explicitly privileged reporting context; tests prove isolation.
API / Component: All analytics endpoints; all repositories and event consumers
Dependencies: IAM tenant claims; tenant context middleware
Notes: Applies to all eight collections, including technical collections.

User Story: As an Academic Admin, I want institution-wide dashboards and policy-controlled exports so that I can monitor academic performance within my permitted scope.
Acceptance Criteria: Institution scope is permitted only for authorized Academic Admins; restricted metrics are separately authorized; export permissions are policy-checked; denied decisions return 403 and are audited.

User Story: As a Department Head, I want analytics limited to my department so that I can review department, batch, subject, and faculty performance without seeing unrelated departments.
Acceptance Criteria: Department scope is resolved from trusted role assignments; requested scopeId is checked against that assignment; cross-department requests return 403; permitted results contain only authorized scope data.

User Story: As a Faculty member, I want analytics for my assigned subjects and batches so that I can monitor attendance and academic progress within my teaching responsibilities.
Acceptance Criteria: Only assigned scopes are returned; unassigned batch/subject IDs are denied; restricted individual-level metrics require additional policy authorization; access decisions are auditable.

User Story: As an authorized Student or Parent, I want only policy-permitted personal or published academic analytics so that I can view relevant information without accessing other people's records.
Acceptance Criteria: Student scope is limited to self; Parent scope is limited to an explicitly authorized student; unpublished or restricted metrics are withheld; exports remain restricted unless policy explicitly allows them.

User Story: As a user requesting sensitive analytics, I want metric classification and scope-based authorization applied so that confidential and restricted data is disclosed only when permitted.
Acceptance Criteria: Metrics carry or inherit a defined classification; PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, and RESTRICTED controls are applied; unauthorized access returns 403; sensitive queries are logged according to policy.
API / Component: Analytics Application Service; query and export authorization

User Story: As an API consumer, I want validated date ranges, filters, deterministic sorting, and bounded query limits so that analytics requests are predictable and safe.
Acceptance Criteria: Invalid dates, reversed ranges, unsupported filters, excessive ranges, or invalid sort keys return 400; maximum ranges and row limits are configurable; list results use deterministic sorting; production dashboard paths use indexed projections.
API / Component: All GET analytics endpoints; API validation layer

User Story: As an API consumer, I want consistent versioned API responses and actionable errors so that clients can handle failures reliably.
Acceptance Criteria: The five canonical endpoints are versioned; errors include code, message, and correlationId; documented cases map to 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500, or 503 as applicable; internal diagnostics are not leaked.
Notes: Canonical detailed-design routes use /api/v1/academics/analytics/*; architecture image also lists /api/v1/reports, /dashboards, /kpis and /analytics/*.

User Story: As an authorized user, I want a role-filtered academic dashboard so that I can see current KPIs for my permitted organizational scope.
Acceptance Criteria: GET dashboard accepts period and scope; response includes only authorized scope metrics; includes attendance, timetable utilization, active course/batch measures where available; response includes asOf and projectionLagSeconds or equivalent freshness metadata.
Source Traceability: Design §§14–16; image API and dashboard sections

User Story: As a Management user, I want institution-approved executive and aggregated trends so that I can review academic performance without unnecessary individual-level data.
Acceptance Criteria: Management views return only authorized executive/aggregated metrics; individual-level restricted data is excluded; filters cannot widen the user's authorized scope; freshness is shown.
Source Traceability: Design §§5, 49–50; image report types and RBAC

User Story: As an authorized academic user, I want attendance analytics by batch, subject, faculty, and date range so that I can identify attendance patterns.
Acceptance Criteria: Endpoint filters by authorized batch and date range; response groups counts by subject and includes present, absent, and percentage values; totals and percentages follow the approved denominator definition; freshness is returned.
Dependencies: ACD-06 AttendanceMarked events; academic calendar context

User Story: As an authorized user, I want attendance shortage risk signals alongside attendance summaries so that I can identify batches or subjects requiring follow-up.
Acceptance Criteria: Configured shortage threshold is applied to sufficiently fresh metrics; risk level is stored with the projection; stale metrics do not trigger a new risk alert; repeated unchanged risk states do not create alert storms.

User Story: As an authorized user, I want timetable utilization by room, faculty, batch, and slot type so that I can understand use of scheduled academic resources.
Acceptance Criteria: Endpoint supports date range and department scope; response includes scheduled, executed, and cancelled slot counts and utilization; configured policy defines denominator treatment for cancelled, substituted, or rescheduled sessions; unauthorized scopes are denied.
Dependencies: ACD-05 TimetablePublished and approved realization/cancellation events; ACD-07 calendar

User Story: As a permitted user, I want underutilized rooms and faculty/resource summaries so that I can investigate utilization patterns.
Acceptance Criteria: Results are grouped by permitted scope; underutilization thresholds are configurable; response identifies resource type, reference, and utilization; missing or stale projections are identified rather than silently treated as zero.

User Story: As an authorized user, I want course, curriculum, and assessment coverage analytics so that I can track academic progression against approved plans.
Acceptance Criteria: Endpoint supports batch and academic period; response includes course completion, curriculum coverage, assessment coverage, and period trend where data exists; calculations use approved upstream events and do not invent unsupported completion facts.
Dependencies: ACD-01 CourseCreated; ACD-02 CurriculumPublished; ACD-04 BatchCreated; ACD-09 AssessmentMappingPublished

User Story: As an authorized user, I want progression risk indicators based on configured targets so that I can identify courses or batches falling behind.
Acceptance Criteria: Configured period targets and deterministic rule versions are applied; risk level and asOf are persisted; only supported facts contribute; threshold crossings or risk-state transitions generate the appropriate insight event.

User Story: As an authorized analytics user, I want approved role/group engagement aggregates so that I can understand report or dashboard consumption without collecting unnecessary personal behavior.
Acceptance Criteria: Only explicitly approved metric types are stored; records are aggregated by audienceType, scopeRef, metricType, and periodKey; raw personal behavior is not stored unless policy requires it; classification and scope checks are enforced.
Dependencies: Approved privacy policy and event source

User Story: As an authorized report designer, I want reusable report definitions and approved templates so that users can generate consistent standard or custom reports.
Acceptance Criteria: A definition includes a stable identifier, name, code, description, type, parameters, system flag, creator, and timestamps; required parameters and allowed filters are validated; only authorized roles can create or update custom definitions.
API / Component: Report definition component; gateway report routes if implemented
MongoDB Collections: Report definitions are shown in the architecture image but are not among the eight collections in the detailed design.
Source Traceability: Architecture image: report_definitions; responsibilities: standard/custom report templates
Notes: Implementation gap: the detailed-design collection inventory has eight collections but no report_definitions collection. Decide whether definitions are configuration, stored elsewhere, or require an approved schema change.

User Story: As the event consumer, I want to consume supported academic domain events from the event bus so that analytics projections remain decoupled from operational services.
Acceptance Criteria: Consumer supports CourseCreated, CurriculumPublished, BatchCreated, TimetablePublished, AttendanceMarked, AcademicCalendarPublished, and AssessmentMappingPublished; it validates event envelopes and tenant context; it does not query upstream operational databases.
Dependencies: Event bus; producer contracts from ACD-01/02/04/05/06/07/09

User Story: As the analytics pipeline, I want heterogeneous source events normalized into canonical analytical facts so that metrics can be calculated consistently across services.
Acceptance Criteria: Each accepted fact stores tenantId, sourceEventId/type/service, entity type/id, occurredAt, processedAt, factType, schemaVersion, and classification; applicable subject/course/batch/faculty/term references and dimensions/measures are populated; source ownership remains upstream.

User Story: As the event consumer, I want duplicate event delivery to be idempotent so that retries do not inflate counts or duplicate facts.
Acceptance Criteria: Uniqueness of tenantId plus sourceEventId is enforced; duplicate deliveries do not change aggregate totals twice; processing outcome is recorded using idempotency controls; concurrent duplicate deliveries are safely handled.

User Story: As the event consumer, I want late and out-of-order events handled through targeted recomputation so that analytical projections remain accurate.
Acceptance Criteria: Events inside the configured recomputation window are accepted; affected aggregates are recomputed rather than destructively overwritten; projection versions increase monotonically; events outside policy are quarantined or handled according to documented retention/reconciliation rules.

User Story: As an operator, I want malformed or non-retryable events quarantined with diagnostics so that poison messages do not block unrelated processing.
Acceptance Criteria: Invalid envelopes and schema/business failures are sent to the dead-letter collection with event identity, source, payload, failure code/message, attempt count, and timestamps; raw payload is not exposed to ordinary business users; unrelated partitions continue processing.

User Story: As an operator, I want authorized replay of dead-letter events so that recoverable failures can be corrected without duplicating analytics.
Acceptance Criteria: Replay requires a privileged role and an audit record; replay status changes are tracked; original event identity is preserved; replay is idempotent; events can be marked replayed or abandoned with reason.

User Story: As an operator, I want event consumer lag and processing failures monitored so that stale analytics and pipeline incidents can be detected.
Acceptance Criteria: Metrics expose consumer lag, processed/failed counts, throughput, and projection freshness; alerts can be configured against operational SLAs; logs include eventId, correlationId, tenantId, duration, and projectionVersion without leaking sensitive payloads.

User Story: As an operator, I want source event schemas and versions validated so that incompatible event changes do not silently corrupt analytics.
Acceptance Criteria: Each event envelope has required eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, version, correlationId, tenant context, and applicable causationId; unsupported schema versions are rejected or quarantined; compatible changes are contract-tested.

User Story: As the projection engine, I want attendance aggregates updated from normalized facts so that attendance queries are fast and consistent.
Acceptance Criteria: Projection keys include tenant, period, batch, subject, faculty, and date bucket as applicable; counters cannot be negative; percentage is between 0 and 100; unique aggregate keys prevent duplicate projection documents; projection version and freshness are updated.

User Story: As the projection engine, I want academic progression aggregates updated from course, curriculum, batch, and assessment events so that coverage trends are available.
Acceptance Criteria: Projection stores period and applicable course/subject/batch/curriculum/assessment references; completion and coverage values are derived only from supported facts; unique aggregate keys and indexes support common queries; version increments monotonically.

User Story: As the projection engine, I want timetable utilization aggregates updated from timetable and calendar events so that utilization can be queried without scanning raw events.
Acceptance Criteria: Projection supports period, batch, room, faculty, and slot type dimensions; scheduled/executed/cancelled counts are non-negative; utilization follows configured business definition; freshness and version are recorded.
Dependencies: ACD-05 timetable; ACD-07 calendar; approved slot outcome events

User Story: As an operator, I want projections rebuilt from retained events or an approved data pipeline so that corrupted or stale read models can be recovered.
Acceptance Criteria: Rebuild runs in an isolated staging projection or versioned rebuild; event replay does not corrupt live reads; record counts and metric invariants are validated; cutover occurs only after validation; rebuild operation is audited.
Dependencies: Retained event stream/data lake; operator authorization

User Story: As an operator, I want projection freshness and version metadata exposed so that users and support teams can distinguish delayed analytics from missing data.
Acceptance Criteria: Each projection exposes asOf, updatedAt, and projectionVersion; dashboard responses expose freshness or lag; stale-projection SLA violations are observable; caches invalidate or expire when projection version changes.
API / Component: Projection metadata; dashboard APIs; cache layer

User Story: As an operator, I want projection updates and corresponding output-event records committed atomically where supported so that downstream consumers are not notified of uncommitted metrics.
Acceptance Criteria: Projection changes and associated outbox record are committed in one MongoDB transaction where transaction boundaries are appropriate; cross-service transactions are not used; failed transactions leave neither a partial projection update nor an orphan event.

User Story: As an authorized administrator, I want KPI and risk thresholds configurable by institution, academic year, or policy so that calculations reflect approved institutional rules.
Acceptance Criteria: Rules are versioned; threshold changes are authorized and auditable; calculation output records the rule/version where required; deterministic baseline calculations can be reproduced.
API / Component: Metric Engine; Risk/Insight Engine; rule configuration

User Story: As a downstream consumer, I want AcademicMetricCalculated events published when approved metrics are recalculated so that BI and intelligence services can consume governed metrics.
Acceptance Criteria: Event contains eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, tenantId, version, correlationId, entity identity, and metric data; event is published through the outbox after commit; consumers can deduplicate it.

User Story: As a downstream notification consumer, I want AttendanceRiskDetected events only when a risk state transitions into an alert condition so that users are not flooded with duplicate alerts.
Acceptance Criteria: Event is emitted when configured threshold and freshness checks pass and risk state transitions; deduplication window suppresses repeated unchanged states; event includes tenant/scope and correlation metadata.
Dependencies: Attendance projection; risk rules; CAM/notification consumer

User Story: As a downstream BI consumer, I want TimetableUtilizationCalculated events published after utilization recalculation so that resource analytics can be integrated without querying ACD-10 MongoDB.
Acceptance Criteria: Event contains metric scope, value/measures, freshness, tenant and correlation metadata; it is reliably published through outbox; consumers use the event/data feed rather than direct database access.

User Story: As an intelligence consumer, I want validated AcademicInsightGenerated events so that higher-level intelligence services can consume governed insights.
Acceptance Criteria: Insight is generated from approved facts and versioned rules; required event envelope fields are present; publication is reliable and deduplicable; only authorized/approved insight content is published.

User Story: As an authorized user, I want to request a report export with a report type, format, and filters so that I can obtain a controlled copy of analytical results.
Acceptance Criteria: POST export validates report type, format, filter schema, tenant, scope, date range, and row limits; request is authorized before job creation; large exports return 202 with jobId, QUEUED status, and poll URI; repeated command with same idempotency key does not create duplicate jobs.
MongoDB Collections: idempotency_records; outbox_events (if events are emitted); metric collections
Dependencies: Export policy; object storage; idempotency key

User Story: As the export worker, I want report jobs processed asynchronously from indexed projections so that large reports do not block interactive APIs.
Acceptance Criteria: Job progresses through REQUESTED/QUEUED/RUNNING to COMPLETED or FAILED/EXPIRED; worker uses indexed projections and bounded filters; retries are controlled; job status and timing are persisted; interactive APIs return promptly.
MongoDB Collections: Architecture image: report_executions; detailed design does not define a report job collection.
Dependencies: Job persistence; worker queue; metric projections
Notes: Implementation gap: report_executions is shown in the image, while the detailed design describes ReportJob but omits a report-job collection from its eight-collection inventory. Confirm the persistence model.

User Story: As an export worker, I want sensitive fields filtered according to the caller's policy so that generated files do not disclose unauthorized data.
Acceptance Criteria: Authorization and field-level policy are re-evaluated at job execution or a documented authorization snapshot is used; output contains only allowed fields and scopes; unauthorized jobs fail safely and are audited.
MongoDB Collections: Metric collections; export job store if approved

User Story: As a report requester, I want to check the status of my export job so that I know whether the report is queued, running, complete, failed, or expired.
Acceptance Criteria: Status lookup verifies tenant and requester/role scope; unknown or unauthorized job access does not disclose job details; response includes status, timestamps, and permitted error information; completed jobs expose a controlled output reference and expiry.
API / Component: GET export job status; image shows /api/v1/reports/{id}/status
MongoDB Collections: Report job persistence is not included in the eight detailed-design collections.
Notes: The exact status route is not specified in the detailed design; map image route to the canonical versioned API contract.

User Story: As a report requester, I want completed exports delivered through controlled, expiring object-storage references so that files are not stored indefinitely in MongoDB or exposed publicly.
Acceptance Criteria: Binary artifacts are stored outside MongoDB; access is authorized and audited; expiry is enforced; expired links/files are inaccessible; output references are tenant-bound and not guessable.
API / Component: Export Service; object storage; download endpoint
MongoDB Collections: Report job persistence is not included in the eight detailed-design collections.

User Story: As an auditor, I want export requests, authorization decisions, completions, downloads, and failures recorded so that report access is traceable.
Acceptance Criteria: Audit entries capture requester, tenant, scope, report type, filters or safe filter summary, decision, timestamps, correlationId, result, and artifact expiry; audit is append-only and access-controlled; secrets and unnecessary sensitive values are excluded.
MongoDB Collections: No dedicated audit collection is included in the eight-collection inventory.
Notes: The architecture image includes report_executions/report_outputs; detailed design requires auditing but does not specify a dedicated audit collection.

User Story: As an operator, I want failed export jobs to retain a safe diagnostic and support controlled retry so that transient failures can be recovered.
Acceptance Criteria: Failure marks the job FAILED with a normalized error code and safe diagnostic; retries follow bounded policy; repeated retries do not create duplicate artifacts; retry and final outcome are auditable.
MongoDB Collections: Report job persistence not specified in the eight-collection inventory; idempotency_records

User Story: As a report requester, I want to export supported reports in approved formats such as PDF, XLSX, and CSV so that I can use the results in institutional workflows.
Acceptance Criteria: Only configured formats are accepted; unsupported formats return 400; file content matches selected filters and authorized scope; generated file metadata records format, size/type where available, creation and expiry.
MongoDB Collections: Report job/output metadata model to be confirmed
Notes: Format list is illustrated in the image; detailed design example explicitly shows XLSX.

User Story: As the event publisher, I want publication intent persisted in an outbox with metric changes so that committed analytics events are not lost.
Acceptance Criteria: Outbox records contain unique eventId, tenantId, eventType, aggregate identity, payload, status, attempt count, and timestamps; publication is retried; successful publication records publishedAt; unique eventId is enforced.

User Story: As an operator, I want failed outbox publications retried with bounded backoff so that temporary event-bus failures recover without manual data repair.
Acceptance Criteria: Pending/failed records are retried according to nextAttemptAt and bounded exponential backoff with jitter; attemptCount increments; permanently failed items are observable and handled by policy; duplicate downstream delivery is safe.

User Story: As a client or event consumer, I want idempotency records to protect repeated commands and event deliveries so that retries do not duplicate effects.
Acceptance Criteria: Record key includes tenantId, idempotencyKey, and operation; requestHash detects key reuse with a different payload; status transitions are controlled; completed responses can be referenced; expiry follows configured retention policy and TTL behavior.
API / Component: Idempotency middleware; export command; event consumer

User Story: As an operator, I want failed events stored with normalized diagnostics and replay status so that failures can be investigated and resolved.
Acceptance Criteria: DLQ record preserves tenantId, eventId/type, source service, payload, failure code/message, attempt count, first/last failure times, replayStatus, and createdAt; unique tenant/event key prevents duplicate DLQ records; replay history is auditable.

User Story: As the service, I want MongoDB schemas and indexes to enforce analytical data integrity so that invalid or duplicate data cannot corrupt reports.
Acceptance Criteria: Required fields and types are validated; tenantId and schemaVersion are present where required; IDs are immutable; counters are non-negative; percentages stay within defined bounds; compound unique indexes enforce aggregate keys; indexes support documented query patterns.
Dependencies: MongoDB schema validators and index migrations

User Story: As a data-governance operator, I want retention and archival policies applied by data class and institution so that analytics data is retained only as long as approved.
Acceptance Criteria: Retention periods are configurable rather than hard-coded; idempotency TTL follows policy; facts can be archived to an approved data-lake tier; DLQ records remain until resolved/closed and then archived; export artifacts expire according to policy.
MongoDB Collections: analytics_facts; idempotency_records; dead_letter_events; outbox_events; external artifact storage

User Story: As a platform operator, I want recoverable backups and a documented restore sequence so that analytics can be restored after data loss or infrastructure failure.
Acceptance Criteria: Backups and point-in-time recovery are configured where supported; recovery restores MongoDB and event processing in documented order; offsets and projection versions are reconciled; critical exports can be regenerated; recovery is tested.
API / Component: Database operations; event consumer; projection rebuild
MongoDB Collections: All 8 collections; retained event stream/data lake

User Story: As a dashboard user, I want common dashboard reads served from indexed projections and appropriately scoped caches so that responses remain fast without exposing stale or cross-tenant data.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard paths do not scan raw facts; normal indexed API P95 target is below 300 ms and indexed analytical query P95 below 2 seconds under agreed test conditions; cache keys include tenant and authorization scope; projection version/asOf informs invalidation; sensitive metrics are not cached unrestricted.

User Story: As an operator, I want service, database, export, and projection health metrics so that reliability and performance issues can be diagnosed.
Acceptance Criteria: Telemetry includes dashboard P95, MongoDB query latency, export queue depth/failure rate, consumer lag, events processed/failed, rebuild duration, projection freshness, and risk-event counts; logs correlate operations with correlationId and tenant context while protecting sensitive data.
API / Component: Observability Layer; API and worker instrumentation

User Story: As a user, I want analytics failures to degrade safely without blocking operational academic transactions so that core academic workflows continue when ACD-10 is unavailable.
Acceptance Criteria: Upstream services do not synchronously depend on ACD-10; dashboard/query outages return controlled errors; event ingestion retries or buffers according to policy; recovery catches up from retained events; service availability target is measured against the agreed 99.9% objective.
Dependencies: Event bus retention; retry and recovery design

User Story: As a downstream BI or intelligence consumer, I want governed metrics and published events/data feeds so that I can consume analytics without querying ACD-10's MongoDB directly.
Acceptance Criteria: Approved consumers receive documented event/data contracts; events include tenant, version, scope, metric and correlation metadata; access is authenticated and authorized; no downstream consumer is granted direct operational access to ACD-10 MongoDB.
Dependencies: Consumer contracts; event bus or approved data pipeline

User Story: As a QA engineer, I want unit, repository, contract, integration, replay, performance, security, data-quality, and disaster-recovery tests so that ACD-10 meets its production acceptance criteria.
Acceptance Criteria: Tests cover deterministic calculations, thresholds, validators, tenant isolation, indexes, REST/event contracts, MongoDB plus event bus/outbox, duplicate/late/out-of-order replay, dashboard P95, export authorization, restore, count reconciliation, and metric invariants; release is blocked on critical failures.
Dependencies: Test environments; representative fixtures; load/security tooling

User Story: As an API platform owner, I want the architecture-image route families mapped to the detailed-design canonical endpoints so that clients use a consistent, documented contract.
Acceptance Criteria: A route map documents /api/v1/reports, /api/v1/dashboards, /api/v1/kpis, /api/v1/analytics/attendance, /performance, /enrolment, /exports, and /schedules against canonical ACD-10 routes or explicitly approved separate APIs; unsupported routes are not exposed; OpenAPI and gateway configuration agree.
API / Component: API Gateway route configuration; OpenAPI specification
Notes: The image and detailed design use different route naming. This story makes that discrepancy an explicit design decision rather than silently assuming equivalence.
